threads.thread_goal: Align on MVP scope, metrics, and event tracking spec before implementation starts.

messages.text: Team, kicking off the Unified Analytics Platform MVP. The main goal is to get a solid foundation in place within the next 3 weeks. Before we start on implementation, we need to align on two key documents. Please review the proposed event tracking spec in A1 and the MVP metrics list in A2. The goal is to get sign-off on both by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks for kicking this off. I've done a quick pass on A1 and A2. The structure for the events looks solid. One question on A2: for the 'feature adoption' metric, are we calculating it as a percentage of total active users or just a raw count?
Looking at A1, for the 'screen_view' event, should we include the user's IP address as a property? It might be useful for location analysis later.

Good question, but we need to be careful with PII. One of the project constraints is to only use anonymised data. Let's stick to the properties defined in A1 for now to avoid any privacy compliance issues.
For 'feature adoption', let's define it as a percentage of monthly active users to normalize it across products. I'll update A2 to make that explicit.
Sorry for the delay. I've read through A1. The naming convention seems clear. Will this spec be enforced automatically or is it just a guideline for now?
Sounds good, thanks for clarifying.

I've reviewed both docs. The event schema in A1 is well-defined and covers the requirements for the metrics in A2. It's also scalable enough that we won't have to redo it for v2. I support signing off on it.
For the MVP, it will be a guideline enforced during code review for T1. We can build automated validation later if we see inconsistencies.
Ok, that makes sense. No PII. The rest of A1 looks fine to me then.

Excellent. It sounds like we have consensus from everyone. Let's make it official.

Decision: We approve the final list of MVP metrics and dashboards as specified in the updated A2. (D1)
Decision: We are signing off on the unified event tracking schema and conventions in A1. (D2)

I'll take on T1 to finalize the spec doc and share it with the product teams.

threads.thread_goal: Converge on architecture and pipeline design for ingestion and transformations.

messages.text: Alright, with the event spec locked, let's finalize the architecture. I've created a draft design doc in A3. It proposes a standard batch processing architecture using our existing cloud services. For the MVP, I suggest we stick to a daily refresh frequency to keep things simple and reliable. Please share your feedback.

Read through A3. Using our existing ingestion streams and orchestrator makes a lot of sense. It means we can reuse our current CI/CD setup for T7, which is a big win. Daily refresh is fine for the MVP dashboards. I'm on board.
I was wondering, would it be possible to do near-real-time updates? Some teams might want to see data that is more up-to-date than 24 hours.

That's a valid point, but streaming architecture adds significant complexity around monitoring, cost, and handling late-arriving data. Given our 21-day deadline and MVP constraints, a daily batch approach (as outlined in A3) is much lower risk. We can definitely add streaming to the v2 backlog.

The architecture in A3 looks good. For the transformation jobs in T3, we should be sure to define clear data quality checks. Things like row count validations and checking for unexpected nulls will be important for building trust in the data.

The batch pattern in A3 is the right call for the MVP. My main comment is on T4. We need a clear versioning strategy for the data models. If we change a table that feeds a dashboard, we need a way to do it without breaking things for consumers of the API or dashboard. We should add a section on this to A3.

Excellent point, @155243. That's a critical detail. I'll add a section to A3 on our versioning approach for semantic models. We'll start with simple view-based versioning (e.g., `v1_users`, `v2_users`).
And yes, @30972, data quality checks are non-negotiable. The definition of done for T3 explicitly includes them.
Ok, daily refresh for MVP makes sense then.

Great discussion. I've updated A3 with the versioning note. Let's formalize the decisions.

Decision: We will adopt the batch processing architecture as documented in A3 for ingestion (T2) and transformation (T3). (D3)
Decision: We will proceed with a daily refresh frequency for all MVP data pipelines. (D4)

This unblocks work on T2, T3, and T4. I'll start scaffolding the ingestion pipeline.

threads.thread_goal: Define dashboard layout, KPIs, and performance expectations for the UI.

messages.text: Hey team, I've put together some initial dashboard wireframes in A8 based on the approved metrics from A2. Let me know your thoughts on the layout, charts, and the proposed filters (product selector and date range).
The layout looks clean. Can we make the line chart for DAU a different color? Maybe blue?
I like the structure. For the date range filter, will it be presets like 'Last 30 Days' or a full calendar picker? A calendar picker might be more flexible.

A full calendar picker can lead to very heavy, slow queries. One of our key constraints is a sub-5-second load time. For the MVP, let's stick to presets ('7d', '30d', '90d'). This will help us meet the performance targets for T11. We can add custom ranges post-launch.

This looks great. One small suggestion: we should add a 'Data updated as of: YYYY-MM-DD' timestamp somewhere visible on the dashboard. Since the data is refreshed daily, it's important to be transparent about its freshness.
Great idea, @155243. I'll add that to the header in A8. And I agree with @96134 on the filters, let's stick to presets. @8323, we can create a ticket for UI theme improvements in the v2 backlog.

Perfect. With those clarifications, I think we're ready to lock this in and start on T5.

Decision: The initial set of dashboard views and filters for the MVP is approved as per the updated wireframes in A8. (D5)
Decision: We confirm the performance targets of <5 second load times for standard queries and daily data freshness. (D6)

threads.thread_goal: Agree on access control, anonymisation, and compliance requirements.

messages.text: Hi team, as part of T8, I've drafted the Data Access and Anonymisation Policy in A5. It defines two access roles (Viewer, Admin) and lists the fields to be anonymised before they land in the warehouse. This is a critical step for security and privacy compliance. Please review so we can get sign-off.
Thanks for putting this together. The policy in A5 is clear and the roles seem appropriate. This maps well to our existing cloud IAM groups, so implementation should be straightforward.
Just to be sure, does this mean we won't have access to raw user IDs in the analytics database at all? What if we need it for debugging a specific user's data?

That's correct. As per the project constraints and the policy in A5, no PII will be available in the analytics environment. All user identifiers will be anonymised (e.g., hashed or replaced with a pseudonym). Debugging will have to be done on aggregated data or by correlating anonymised IDs with production logs, which is outside the scope of this platform's access model.
The policy looks solid. We should make sure the process for requesting access is documented in the operational runbook (A6) as part of T9.
Good point, @30972. I'll add a note to T9 to ensure we link to A5 from the runbook and document the access request flow.
Understood. The policy is fine with me then.

Thanks for the quick feedback, everyone. It seems we are all aligned on the approach.

Decision: We approve the data access roles and anonymisation rules as described in A5. (D7)

I will now forward this to the security officer for their final review to complete T8.

threads.thread_goal: Plan launch, validate readiness, and capture follow-ups after MVP go-live.

messages.text: Team, we're in the home stretch. I've updated the MVP Launch Readiness Checklist in A4. All core development and testing tasks are marked as complete. The only major outstanding item is the historical data backfill (T10), which is currently running. I'm proposing we launch this Friday, pending a green light on the backfill. Please review A4 and raise any final concerns.
Just reviewed A4. All my items related to monitoring and CI/CD are green. The operational runbook A6 is also ready for handover. Friday works for me. Great progress!

Quick update on T10: the backfill job (tracked in A7) is about 80% complete and running smoothly. I've done some spot checks on the loaded data and counts match the source. It should be fully complete and validated by tomorrow afternoon. I see no blockers for a Friday launch.
This is great news. Who will be leading the handover demo session mentioned in T12?
I can help prepare the slides and talking points for the demo if that's helpful.
@8323, I'll lead the demo, but we should all be there to answer questions. @30972, that would be a great help, thank you. Let's sync up tomorrow morning to outline the T12 demo flow.

Okay, with the positive status on the backfill and no blockers raised against A4, I'm making the call. We are GO for launch.

Decision: The MVP launch date is confirmed for this Friday. (D8)

Fantastic work everyone. I'll schedule the T12 handover session and send out the launch announcement. Let's get this shipped!
